ab_beach_front_buttress.blurb: A small satellite crag in the Moose Mountain climbing area of Kananaskis, Alberta, and the first cliff you meet when heading up Canyon Creek. It holds 13 bolted sport routes on limestone, none much taller than a rope-stretch of 20 m. Most lines fall in the 5.10 range, with one in the 5.8 to 5.9 bracket each and a handful of 5.11s, so it suits climbers working through the lower double digits and anyone wanting a quick warm-up. The wall faces south and stays sunny and sheltered from wind, which makes it a pleasant choice in late winter and early spring. A sandy beach lies beneath the face. The walk from the road is short.

ab_bench.blurb: One of the sport crags in the Moose Mountain area of Kananaskis, Alberta, set along the Canyon Creek valley road west of Calgary. The area is built on limestone, and this crag offers 14 bolted routes. The grades cluster hard in one band: ten of the climbs are 5.10, with a single 5.7, a single 5.8 and a pair of 5.9s making up the easier end. That makes it a good fit for climbers already comfortable on 5.10 who want a quiet, mid-sized spot rather than the busiest walls of the valley. Expect limestone that can vary in quality from route to route.

ab_david_thompson_highway.blurb: A winter ice climbing corridor on Highway 11 between Saskatchewan Crossing and Nordegg, reached by leaving the Icefields Parkway at the Crossing. Its 14 climbs are almost all frozen waterfalls: about a dozen are graded WI3 to WI5, with the bulk at WI4, plus a single mixed line near M6. Routes run from single pitches to multi-pitch outings, and the valley is generally quieter than the better-known Rockies ice venues. The season runs from late fall to early spring. Short winter days and snow-covered trails mean a late-morning start and sturdy boots or snowshoes are worth planning for.
